h: Apple to replace iPhone Duo units with cracked inner screens
s: Buyers of Apple's first foldable reported cracks and dead pixels near the hinge within days; the company has not explained the fault.

h: Netherlands reverses course and pulls out of Eurovision 2027 over Israel
s: Dutch public broadcaster NPO said the 'sensitivities' around Israel's participation had not gone away, a month after announcing a careful return.

h: Likud readies fraud complaints over Arab polling stations, reports say
s: Hebrew media say party activists discussed a 'stolen election' campaign if Netanyahu loses; the elections committee says there is no evidence of widespread fraud.

h: Palestinian youth shot in the foot near Huwara checkpoint
s: Red Crescent medics said Israeli forces at first kept their crews from reaching the wounded young man south of Nablus before letting them through.

h: Six-year-old girl dies of gunshot wounds in al-Mawasi
s: Tihani Shalalfeh was shot by Israeli forces in the coastal area west of Khan Younis and died on Tuesday morning, WAFA reported, as firing continued in central and southern Gaza.

h: From a Rafah tent to the national team: Mohammed Balah's Asian Cup hopes
s: The 33-year-old striker, once called the 'Ronaldo of Gaza', returned to Palestine's squad in June after 2,495 days, the longest gap between caps in the team's history.

h: Gaza-born actor Iyad Hajjaj's short film reaches 19 awards
s: My Foot is in Heaven, about a Gaza father whose daughter's foot must be amputated without anaesthetic, was shot in southern California on a set built to look like Gaza.

h: Jordan strikes armed groups in Syria over Karak church attack
s: Jordan's air force said it hit groups linked to Friday's deadly attack; Syria said seven civilians, including three children, were killed in Daraa and Sweida.

h: Settlers burn three cars and spray slogans in Umm Safa overnight
s: The head of the Umm Safa village council said settlers entered the western neighbourhood after midnight, set three vehicles alight and daubed racist slogans on walls.

h: Two families ordered out of their homes in Far'un as troops take them over
s: Israeli forces turned two houses south of Tulkarem into military posts and told the families they could not return until Wednesday morning, local sources told WAFA.

h: Harry Kane wins the Ballon d'Or ahead of Mbappé and Yamal
s: The Bayern Munich striker, 33, is the first English winner in about 25 years after 61 goals in 51 club games; Alexia Putellas won the women's award for a third time.

h: Sixty MEPs urge emergency EU meeting on sanctions against Israel
s: In a letter to Kaja Kallas, lawmakers from several groups called the West Bank blockade collective punishment and cited Hebron families given minutes to leave.

h: Israelis vote in a close election for the 26th Knesset
s: Polls show Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition both short of 61 seats; turnout at 10am was the highest for that hour since 1981. Exit polls are due at 10pm.

h: Israeli forces close every entrance to Ramallah on election morning
s: Gates and checkpoints around Ramallah were shut from early Tuesday and new checkpoints went up on the side roads residents use to get around them, WAFA reported.

h: Israel turns back 23-member delegation heading to Birzeit conference
s: British and Spanish lawmakers were among those held for hours at the Allenby Crossing and then refused entry to the West Bank, Birzeit University said.

h: Antonelli wins US Grand Prix and closes in on first F1 title
s: The 20-year-old Mercedes driver won from pole in Austin for his ninth victory of the season and now leads George Russell by 123 points with five races left.

h: New York Times rejects UN rapporteur's 'mediacide' report
s: Francesca Albanese accused major outlets of helping legitimise Israel's actions in Gaza; the Times said her report offers no proof of outside pressure.

h: Netanyahu pressed for Iran strike before the vote, but Trump said wait — CNN
s: US and Israeli sources told CNN that Washington asked Israel to delay any joint action; the prime minister's office called the report fake news.

h: Abbas meets new Iraqi prime minister in Amman
s: The Palestinian president briefed Ali al-Zaidi on Gaza and the West Bank and on the PA's financial crisis, which he blamed on $7bn in withheld revenues.

h: In Gaza's tents, a kilowatt-hour now costs ten times its pre-war price
s: With the grid destroyed, private generators sell electricity at around 30 shekels per kilowatt-hour, and families who cannot pay are going without light.

h: Palestine to face hosts Saudi Arabia in Asian Cup opener
s: The AFC confirmed the 2027 tournament will go ahead as planned in Saudi Arabia from 7 January, despite postponements of other events over Houthi attacks.

h: Macklemore opens 'Free Palestine' tour in Dublin with Palestinian singer Lina Makhoul
s: The 13,000-seat 3Arena sold out in minutes for the first of three European dates, with Hozier, Kneecap and DJ Habibeats also on the bill.

h: Lula wins fourth term as Bolsonaro's party concedes
s: The leftist incumbent came from behind in the first round to beat Flavio Bolsonaro by about 4.4 million votes in Sunday's runoff.

h: Mecca pact states meet in Tehran as Saudi Arabia downs more Houthi drones
s: Iran held talks with Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey on regional security while the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil stations and Riyadh airport.
p: Tehran, Iran and Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

h: Fire destroys tent camp near Shuja'iyya junction, displacing over 800
s: WAFA said Israeli drones set the camp alight overnight; the UN separately reported arson attacks on families' tents along the Yellow Line in the same area.

h: Qatar and Egypt condemn Ben-Gvir's entry to Al-Aqsa compound
s: The two governments said the visit by Israel's national security minister, escorted by police and joined by hundreds of settlers, breached the status quo at the holy site.

h: Mbappé double gives Real Madrid Clásico win at Camp Nou
s: Real won 2-1 to cut Barcelona's lead at the top of La Liga to three points, with Mbappé's winner coming in the 87th minute.

h: UN inquiry says Israel is still committing genocide in Gaza despite ceasefire
s: The Commission of Inquiry also alleged crimes against humanity in the West Bank; Israel called the report a misinformation campaign and demanded the body be dissolved.

h: Albania signs up to Gaza stabilisation force as deployment stalls
s: Albanian liaison officers are due in the region in November, and Kosovo says its bomb disposal team is ready, but no troops have yet deployed in Gaza.

h: Hezbollah rearming with Iranian cash for possible new war, sources say
s: Lebanese security sources told Reuters the group has used the lull since June to rebuild its drone and explosives capacity, though it is not yet fully prepared.

h: Hebron displacement passes 3,000 as UN rights chief warns of collective punishment
s: Volker Türk called for everyone forced from the Jalda and Ein Deir Baha neighbourhoods to be allowed home, as Palestinian figures put the number displaced near 4,000.

h: Settlers attack olive pickers in Beit Kahil as harvest incidents pass 480
s: A Palestinian commission says it has recorded 482 attacks on the olive harvest in nine West Bank governorates since picking began this month.

h: Boston Palestine Film Festival closes its 20th edition with Palestine Comedy Club
s: Ten days of screenings across Boston ended at the Coolidge Corner Theatre with a documentary following six comedians touring a stand-up show across Palestine.

h: PLO rejects UNRWA layoff plan and seeks $70m to pay staff
s: The PLO Executive Committee says mass job cuts would not fix the agency's finances and asked donors for urgent money to cover November and December salaries.

h: About 70 Palestinians detained across the West Bank since Friday, PPS says
s: The Palestinian Prisoners' Society said most of those held were former prisoners, and that hundreds more had been interrogated in the field during raids.

h: About 1,200 forced from homes as Israel launches Hebron operation
s: The army began house searches and demolitions in two Hebron neighbourhoods after gunmen killed two soldiers at a checkpoint; the PA called it collective punishment.

h: Jerusalem Patriarchate condemns deadly attack on Karak church
s: Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at St George's Greek Orthodox Church in Karak; the Patriarchate said Jordan's Christians would stay in their homeland.

h: Dublin's IMMA opens show of six Gaza artists, some works smuggled out
s: Eltiqa: How to Work Together? brings more than 60 works from 2002 to 2025 by the Gaza City collective to the Irish Museum of Modern Art, with free entry.

h: Palestinian goods trade deficit widens 17% in August
s: Statistics bureau figures show exports to Israel rising while exports to the rest of the world almost halved, deepening dependence on a single market.

h: EBRD and EU open €25.9m green finance line for Palestinian firms and homes
s: Loans through local banks will fund solar, efficiency and waste projects, with EU grants covering up to a quarter of eligible investments.

h: AI-found PHP flaw forces governments to take websites offline
s: OpenAI says one of its models found the 'php2shell' bugs, which allow remote code execution on any PHP server; the Netherlands, France and others pulled services to patch.

h: Five Palestinians drown in two boat incidents off Greek islands
s: The Greek coast guard recovered four bodies near Lesbos and one near Samos; the passengers were Palestinians who had set out from Lebanon and Syria.

h: UN warns of 'ominous start' to the West Bank olive harvest
s: OCHA counted at least 160 harvest-related settler attacks in the first two weeks of October, while movement restrictions keep thousands of farmers from their trees.

h: Oversight Board faults Meta over removal of protest and election accounts
s: The board said 'No Kings' activist accounts and Brazilian election pages were taken down by error and should have been protected by Meta's cross-check system.

h: Palestinian-founded Databuddy raises $500,000 from Y Combinator
s: Issa Nassar's AI product-analytics start-up says it has signed more than 3,000 business customers in its first months.

h: Tech for Palestine and Thaura plan Barcelona hackathon on 'ethical alternatives'
s: The one-day event on 31 October at the Canòdrom, part of Mozilla Festival, asks teams to build tools that help users leave 'complicit technology'.

h: EU weighs Blocking Statute to shield ICC from US sanctions
s: The European Commission says shielding court officials from Washington's measures remains an option, ten days after the US banned transactions with the court.

h: WFP cuts Gaza food aid by a third, leaving 500,000 without support
s: The World Food Programme says funding for its Palestine operations is under half of past years and it needs $450 million to keep going through March.

h: Maryam Bsharat retains world junior karate title
s: The Palestinian beat Spain's Noa López González 3-1 in the under-66kg kumite final and remains world number one in her category.
